editorial:
Devices drops you into one long, sleepless night with a brand-new dad who suddenly has to handle everything alone. His wife is away, the baby is crying, and every helper gadget in the house starts acting like it has its own plans. The movie builds tension from ordinary parenting stress, turning bottle warmers, monitors, and smart speakers into unsettling little threats. You feel the panic of someone who wants to do right by his child but cannot tell what is real and what is exhaustion. The tone is tense without being too bloody, so even horror fans who dislike extreme gore can stay engaged.

The lead performance carries the whole story, showing fear, love, and stubborn determination in small moments. Pacing is brisk, with short scenes that keep you checking every shadow. Some scares are predictable, and a few side characters feel thin, but the emotional core works. If you enjoy home-invasion style horror with a family twist, this is a strong pick. Watch it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the sharpest sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the father discovers the devices were not possessed by a ghost. His wife, trapped by debt and fear, secretly programmed them to push him out of the house and make him look unstable. The baby monitor reveals her voice giving commands. He saves the baby, calls for help, and stays. The last shot shows one device still blinking, suggesting the danger may not be fully over.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family-centered horror with smart-home scares.
